title: Boys Only
subtitle: This is hardly a promised land for the ladies.

items.text: Finding Xavier
Boys Only
The morning sun falls through the window and onto the display cabinet.
The badges stand in line, upright, like little toy soldiers.
Just like the Scout motto says, "Be prepared!"

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: ... In a word—

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: It's against the rules.
The child standing before the Scout leader doesn't respond. She's enraptured by the badges—the representation of a Scout's honor.
Every child who enters this room is attracted to them, but none more so than Eagle.
Her eyes are glued, sparkling with eagerness.

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: Are you listening?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: S-sorry, sir, I ...

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I didn't catch that.

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: I said that girls aren't allowed to join the Scouts. It's against the rules.

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: Go home, kid.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Please, just let me show my skills. Maybe then you'll change your mind. I've been working so hard and—

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: No need to step forward.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Yes, sir.

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: Listen, kid, no girl has ever joined the Scouts, and no girl will ever join the Scouts.

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: Let me see ... You applied 10 days ago, and a month ago, too. Didn't they tell you back then that girls weren't allowed?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Yes, sir, they did ...

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: Well, then it seems you're the problem. You don't remember what people tell you.

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: You've got a short attention span—maybe even some kind of attention deficit. I'm afraid that doesn't meet the Scout's standards.
Eagle didn't expect such a simple mistake to lead to such irreparable consequences.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: But sir, you haven't seen my survival skills presentation—
She won't let this chance slip away from her like this. Not again.

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: I don't need to.

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: Look behind you. There's a whole line of people waiting to speak to me. A Scout must always "help others," remember?
She doesn't need to turn back to know that there's an orderly line of boys behind her, each with their eyes fixed on her.
She lowers her eyes and obediently recites the section of the Scout Oath.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: "... help other people at all times ..."

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: Exactly. If you really want to be a Scout, you should start acting like one.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: But sir—

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: You're also forgetting another law: "A Scout obeys orders." Something you're failing to do right now.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Understood ...

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Sorry, sir.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: It's okay, it's okay ...
She whispers to herself, playing as her own comforter.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: What would Father do if he was rejected?
... Mission ... Find the missing ...
... Chemical plant ...
Fragments of a conversation drift through the partially opened door ahead.
Eagle halts, subconsciously holding her breath to better hear it.
As she carefully draws nearer to the source, the voice becomes clearer.

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: His name is Xavier.

items.speaker: Scout Leader
items.text: I repeat, Xavier was last seen near the chemical plant. Your next mission is to find Xavier and take him back.
Scout Manual, Essential Virtues, Article III: "Be acute and seize opportunities."
TO BE CONTINUED…
